Researchers at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute and IBM T.J.

Watson Research Center published a technical paper titled “REACH: Controller-Managed Long-Span ECC for HBM AI Inference.”
Abstract Excerpt: “High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) cost motivates stronger controller protection...

Long-span error-correcting codes provide stronger protection at a comparable code rate, but a direct implementation couples small accesses to span-wide state and requires costly decoding at HBM bandwidth.
Read-dominated LLM decode offers a favorable setting: sequential reads support span aggregation, while sparse writes limit parity-update traffic.

This paper presents REACH, a controller microarchitecture that uses established inner codes to correct common errors and identify unresolved chunks, reserving a long outer code for known-erasure repair.”

bullets:
News from this week’s SPIE Photomask Technology + Extreme Ultraviolet Lithographyconference:
ASML and TSMC are launching an industry initiative to transition high-NA EUV lithography from current 6-inch photomasks to...
The companies are targeting a 12-inch mask pilot line by 2031, with production-ready systems by 2033.
TSMC plans to begin using high-NA EUV in high-volume manufacturing in 2030.
The eBeam Initiative‘s annual industry survey found 66% of semiconductor experts expect large-format photomasks to be adopted within a decade, while 94% expect mask revenue to grow this year.

imec demonstrated single-exposure high-NA EUV patterning of 22nm-pitch lines/spaces and 28nm-pitch vias using established chemically amplified resist technology, supporting layers envisioned for A14/A10 logic.
